results.question: How can legacy pods without an Istio sidecar connect to a STRICT mTLS service?
results.answer: When an Istio namespace or workload is configured with `PeerAuthentication` in `STRICT` mode, any client connecting over plain unencrypted TCP/HTTP without an authenticated mTLS certificate handshake will be immediately rejected with TCP connection reset or `connection termination`. results.question: What Nginx ingress annotation should be tuned to resolve 504 Gateway Timeout on long-running APIs?
results.answer: HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout occurs when an edge proxy or Kubernetes Ingress Controller (Nginx Ingress, AWS Load Balancer Controller / ALB, Traefik) fails to receive a timely response from an upstream backend service pod within the configured timeout window [kubernetes_ingress_504_gateway_timeout.md#kubernetes_ingress_504_gateway_timeout.md-c0] Heavy database queries, slow external API calls, or garbage collection pauses exceed the default 60-second Nginx `proxy-read-timeout`. - **Immediate Fix:** Add timeout annotations to the Ingress resource: ```yaml metadata: annotations: nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-connect-timeout: "15" nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-read-timeout: "180" nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-send-timeout: "180" ``` For AWS ALB Ingress: ```yaml metadata: annotations: alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/load-balancer-attributes: idle_timeout.timeout_seconds=180 [kubernetes_ingress_504_gateway_timeout.md#kubernetes_ingress_504_gateway_timeout.md-c6] Client sees:** `504 Gateway Time-out` - **Ingress Controller log shows:** `upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream` - **Impact:** Failed API transactions, degraded user checkout/request flows, and customer-facing incident alerts. [kubernetes_ingress_504_gateway_timeout.md#kubernetes_ingress_504_gateway_timeout.md-c0]

results.question: Why do AWS Network Load Balancer target instances register as Target.FailedHealthChecks?
results.answer: When traffic arrives at an AWS Application Load Balancer (ALB) or Network Load Balancer (NLB), target instances or container IPs in the Target Group fail health checks and are marked `Unhealthy`. - **Client sees:** `HTTP 502 Bad Gateway` (ALB) or connection resets / TCP RST (NLB). - **Target Group Console displays:** `Target.FailedHealthChecks` or `HealthCheck.Unhealthy`. - **Impact:** Entire availability zones or backend services become unreachable. [aws_network_load_balancer_unhealthy_hosts.md#aws_network_load_balancer_unhealthy_hosts.md-c0] Check Target Group Health via AWS CLI] [aws_network_load_balancer_unhealthy_hosts.md#aws_network_load_balancer_unhealthy_hosts.md-c1] bash aws elbv2 describe-target-health \ --target-group-arn <target-group-arn> \ --query "TargetHealthDescriptions[].{Target:Target.Id,Port:Target.Port,State:TargetHealth.State,Reason:TargetHealth.Reason,Description:TargetHealth.Description}" \ --output table [aws_network_load_balancer_unhealthy_hosts.md#aws_network_load_balancer_unhealthy_hosts.md-c1]

results.question: How do you triage high queue execution latency for Sidekiq background jobs in GitLab production?
results.answer: Defer execution of all jobs of that class, using either: - Chatops: ```shell /chatops gitlab run feature set run_sidekiq_jobs_Example::SlowWorker false --ignore-feature-flag-consistency-check --ignore-production-check ``` - Rails console: ```ruby Feature.disable(:"run_sidekiq_jobs_Example::SlowWorker") ``` The above action will cause sidekiq workers to defer (rather than execute) all jobs of that class, including jobs currently waiting in the queue [disabling-a-worker.md#disabling-a-worker.md-c0] The [sidekiq: Worker Detail dashboard](https://dashboards.gitlab.net/d/sidekiq-worker-detail/sidekiq3a-worker-detail) may be helpful in checking a worker's enqueue rate, queue size, and summed execution time spent in shared dependencies like the DB [disabling-a-worker.md#disabling-a-worker.md-c0]
